note: Study aids are learner-facing coaching, separate from the source answer, rationale and question text. Each entry stays 'draft' until a person has checked it against the source PDF. 'hints' are shown before reveal and must never name or quote the correct option; 'optionNotes' and 'mnemonic' are shown only after reveal.

associate-1.1.concept: Effective prompts supply what the model cannot guess
hints: For each revision, ask what the model would still have to guess if it received exactly that text.
Cross out revisions that add pressure, repetition, or flattery instead of new information.
The strongest revision states the deliverable, its length, the audience, the tone, and the goal.

optionNotes.A: Asks for 'better' but adds no information the model lacked, so it applies pressure without content.
optionNotes.B: Supplies the deliverable, length, audience, tone, and goal: everything the model could not guess.
optionNotes.C: Repeating the request restates the same missing context; it adds emphasis, not information.
optionNotes.D: A persona flatters the model but still omits audience, format, and purpose, which determine the result.

associate-1.1.mnemonic: Five ingredients: what, how long, who for, what voice, why.

hints: Sort the choices into those that give the model more information about its target and those that withhold it.
Eliminate choices that rely on emphasis or on the model guessing rather than on facts.
Look for one choice about who the text is for and why, and one about the shape the result must take.

optionNotes.A: Deliberate vagueness withholds exactly the information that output quality depends on.
optionNotes.B: Audience and purpose let the model aim at the right target.
optionNotes.C: Capital letters change emphasis, not the model's understanding.
optionNotes.D: Format, length, and tone fix the shape of the deliverable so the draft is usable.
optionNotes.E: Asking the model to guess withholds what only the company knows.

associate-1.7.mnemonic: Aim (who and why) plus shape (format, length, tone).

professional-1.11.concept: Choosing the simplest agentic pattern that fits
hints: For each scenario ask whether the sequence of steps is fixed in advance or decided by what earlier steps reveal.
Count how many distinct specialists, each with their own tools and context, the task needs.
A single transformation with its context supplied needs no orchestration at all.

optionNotes.A: One augmented call suits a single transformation where the needed context is supplied (scenarios 1 and 5).
optionNotes.B: A fixed workflow suits a stable, repeating sequence of steps (scenario 2).
optionNotes.C: An autonomous agent suits a path that depends on what each step reveals (scenario 3).
optionNotes.D: A multi-agent system suits distinct specialists coordinated into one output (scenario 4).

professional-1.11.mnemonic: Climb the ladder only as far as needed: one call, fixed steps, runtime-decided path, many specialists.
